guide.what: The gap between 10-year and 2-year Treasury yields (also shown: 10-year minus 3-month).
read: Upward-sloping (normal) means the market expects expansion; flat means a transition; inverted means it expects a contraction.
The direction of the move matters more than the level: flattening toward inversion is bearish, steepening out of inversion or flatness is bullish.
Check the short end too: in February 2020 only the 3-month part of the curve was inverted.
watch: A transitioning curve has often announced the Fed's next move rather than a crash: read it with real rates, credit and the VIX.
In 2006-07 the 10y-2y spread was negative most of the time before the financial crisis.
